title: Grade 7 Mathematics Scheme of Work: Numbers, Fractions and Percentages (Synthetic Mock Corpus)
subject: Mathematics

learningOutcomes: Identify factors and multiples of given whole numbers
Determine common factors and common multiples of two whole numbers
Apply divisibility rules to identify factors of whole numbers
keyConcepts: A factor divides a number exactly
A multiple is obtained by multiplying a number by a whole number
Common factors and common multiples are shared by two or more numbers
Divisibility rules help determine whether a number is divisible by another number
learningActivities: Learners list factors of selected numbers using multiplication facts
The teacher demonstrates how to find common factors and common multiples
Learners work in pairs to investigate divisibility rules for 2, 3, 5 and 10
Learners solve short problems involving grouping objects into equal groups
entries.assessment: List all factors of 24, identify the common factors of 18 and 24, and state whether 735 is divisible by 5.
entries.teacherNotes: Learners may confuse factors with multiples. Use arrays and equal-grouping activities to demonstrate the difference before introducing abstract exercises.

priorKnowledge: Recognising fractions as parts of a whole
learningOutcomes: Identify equivalent fractions using diagrams and numerical examples
Generate equivalent fractions by multiplying or dividing the numerator and denominator by the same non-zero number
Simplify fractions to their lowest terms using common factors
keyConcepts: Equivalent fractions represent the same value
Multiplying or dividing the numerator and denominator by the same non-zero number preserves a fraction's value
Common factors can be used to simplify fractions
learningActivities: Learners use fraction strips and shaded diagrams to identify equivalent fractions
The teacher demonstrates generating equivalent fractions
Learners simplify fractions using common factors
Learners compare their solutions and explain their methods
entries.assessment: Write two fractions equivalent to 3/5 and simplify 18/24 to its lowest terms.
entries.teacherNotes: Learners may divide only the numerator or denominator when simplifying. Emphasise that both must be divided by the same non-zero factor.

learningOutcomes: Add and subtract fractions with the same denominator
Add fractions with different denominators by finding a common denominator
Solve everyday problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions
keyConcepts: Fractions with different denominators must be expressed using a common denominator before addition or subtraction
Equivalent fractions can be used to obtain a common denominator
Answers should be simplified where possible
learningActivities: The teacher models fraction addition using visual representations
Learners convert fractions to equivalent fractions with common denominators
Groups solve word problems involving measurements and sharing quantities
Learners check their answers and explain their calculations
entries.assessment: Calculate 2/5 + 1/3 and 7/8 - 1/4, showing the working and simplifying the answers.
entries.teacherNotes: Learners may add or subtract denominators directly. Reinforce that the denominator describes the size of the parts and must remain common when combining fractions.

priorKnowledge: Place value in whole numbers and decimal numbers
Understanding fractions as parts of a whole
learningOutcomes: Convert simple fractions into decimals using division
Express decimals as percentages by multiplying by 100
Convert common percentages into equivalent fractions and decimals
keyConcepts: A percentage represents a quantity out of 100
Fractions, decimals and percentages can represent the same value
Equivalent representations can be used to compare quantities
learningActivities: Learners match fraction, decimal and percentage cards representing equivalent values
The teacher demonstrates conversions using place-value charts
Learners convert common fractions such as 1/2, 1/4 and 3/4
Learners complete a conversion table and explain the relationships between representations
entries.assessment: Convert 3/4 into a decimal and a percentage. Express 0.2 as a percentage and as a fraction in its simplest form.
entries.teacherNotes: Some learners may confuse multiplying by 100 with dividing by 100. Use familiar benchmark percentages and visual models to reinforce the relationship.
